John sold some lego sets to buy video games. The total money spent on video games is 8 × $20 = $160, plus $5 left over gives a total of $165 from selling lego sets. Since each lego set sells for $15, the number sold is $165 ÷ $15 = 11. He originally had 13 lego sets, so he still has 13 - 11 = 2 lego sets.

Answer: 2
reasoning:
We are given: "John plans to sell all his toys and use the money to buy video games. He has 13 lego sets and he sells them for $15 each. He ends up buying 8 video games for $20 each and has $5 left. How many lego sets does he still have?"

Interpretation: John initially has 13 lego sets. He plans to sell all his toys, but it says "He ends up buying 8 video games for $20 each and has $5 left. How many lego sets does he still have?" So he presumably sold some lego sets, but not necessarily all? The phrase "He has 13 lego sets and he sells them for $15 each" might mean he sells each lego set for $15, but maybe he only sold some? Then he buys 8 video games at $20 each, and has $5 left. So total money spent on video games is 8*20 = $160, plus $5 left, so total money he had from selling lego sets is $165. Since each lego set sells for $15, the number of lego sets he sold is 165/15 = 11. So he sold 11 lego sets. He originally had 13, so he still has 13 - 11 = 2 lego sets. That seems straightforward.
